## How it works

In the workspace, a harness is one running session of an agent such as Codex or Claude Code, with its own conversation and working context. A tab groups harnesses. Use New Harness to start one and New Tab to group work. Harnesses in the same tab can message each other with `harness send`: Agent Messages, an experiment of your account, off by default and turned on in Settings ▸ Experimental.

The Store offers harnesses with instructions, tools, and optional viewers for specific crafts. Install a harness, then start it in your workspace. See the Naming System for the complete naming rules.

One daemon per machine runs your agents in tmux. It dials out, so no machine opens a port. [...] ## Harness device

Get a Harness device, or build your own from the files below. The firmware guide lists the supported boards and build commands, and the hardware guide covers the design files.

The optional Harness device is a round, always-on display that sits beside your keyboard and shows your agents at a glance: what each one is doing, which one has finished, and which one is waiting on you. Read a question and answer it on the screen, or tap and speak a new task, without switching windows.

It is open hardware, all the way down. This repository has everything it takes to build one: [...] ## Repository files navigation

## What to consider when choosing a Harness alternative

Before switching to another CI/CD tool, consider the following key factors:

What does an Autonomous SDLC actually look like?

Harness founder and CEO Jyoti Bansal explains how Harness is building an Autonomous Software Development Lifecycle where AI agents help take software from idea to production — across planning, coding, testing, security, deployment, runtime protection, and cost management.

As AI coding agents like Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Codex generate more code, the bottleneck is shifting beyond code creation. Harness is focused on everything that happens after the code is written: building, testing, securing, deploying, verifying, protecting, and optimizing software in production. [...] In this keynote, Jyoti breaks down the Harness Autonomous SDLC and the agents powering it, including:

• Software Delivery Agent — builds and safely moves changes to production
• Security Testing Agent — identifies and remediates risk before software ships
• Runtime Protection Agent — protects applications, APIs, and AI in production
• Cost Management Agent — manages cloud, AI, token, and engineering costs

The goal: an idea goes in, working software comes out, with autonomous agents operating across the software delivery lifecycle.
